liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Desolation Row** (4 reviews, 1 other source): Main gate crashing happened during this song; reviewer calls it among the best versions, with Weir engaged and Garcia's pitch bending eerie; Mayhem broke loose soon after Weir sang the verse about the riot squad being restless [5][19][20][21][26]
- **Fire On The Mountain** (1 review, 1 other source): The show turns very dark when Fire On The Mountain moves into Victim Or The Crime; Only the first verse of the song is on this recording [4][24]
- **New Speedway Boogie** (1 review): It nearly takes off like the protest song it was designed to be [21]

## Setlist highlights

- **It's All Too Much**: rare: 6 archived performances [27]

## The recordings

- **gd1995-07-02.aud.unknown.tetzeli.fix-12578.74417.reflac.flac16** (recommended): audience recording; 18 songs; 148 min; rated 1/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd95-07-02.aud.unk.12578.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 18 songs; 148 min; rated 2.86/5 by 36 [2]. Said about its sound: Scarlet Begonias and Fire On The Mountain are split across discs with fades, and Quinn is faded out at the end; Reviewer says the recording may not be the best [18][24]
- **gd1995-07-02.172645.senn.me88.greenberg.roeder.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 18 songs; 150 min [4]
- **gd95-07-02.aud.ball.587.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 18 songs; 148 min; rated 2.37/5 by 46 [3]

## Around the show

- Gatecrashers and disorder marred the night, yet the band played with poise and gave the innocent fans a good show [16]
- Reviewer wonders what the 3rd's show would have been like had the gate crashing not happened [17]
- Reviewer was on the lawn; the next night's show was cancelled, making this their last Dead show [19]
- Reviewer saw crowds come over the fence and sensed this would be their final Dead show [20]
- Crowd surged toward the left side screaming at cops; a man who urged a rush was maced and dragged off [23]
- Night was dark and strange; people can be heard rushing in during Desolation Row [24]
- House lights stayed on all night due to a death threat against Jerry; riots and gate crashers followed [25]
- Reviewer found the show sloppy, with Jerry strung out, and the second night was cancelled [25]
- Reviewer finds it just okay for 1995, with better shows available from that tour [18]
- Reviewer sees the show as symbolic of 1995, with Jerry slipping but the band inspired by the gate crashers [21]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1995-07-02.aud.unknown.tetzeli.fix-12578.74417.reflac.flac16**: taped by unknown; transferred by Bill Tetzeli; source: Unknown AUD>??>Bootleg CD>WAV>SHN>WAV>FLAC [1]
- **gd95-07-02.aud.unk.12578.sbeok.shnf**: source: Bootleg CD>WAV>SHN [2]. Also: Two copies of this audience recording are listed, and the reviewer cannot tell whether they differ; This copy is a liberated silver CD called "Big Bust", probably the same source as the other listed version [17][18]
- **gd1995-07-02.172645.senn.me88.greenberg.roeder.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Jason Greenberg and Terry Roeder; transferred by Jason Greenberg, Charlie Miller, Scott Clugston; source: Master Audience DAT; Sennheiser ME-88 mics (on the lawn) > Sony TC-D7 (16-bit/48k) [4]
- **gd95-07-02.aud.ball.587.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience: Unknown Mics [3]
